# tboardfs mounted logs

This read-only tree exposes TensorBoard event data as files for training analysis. A log-directory mount has one directory per run; a run-directory mount exposes that run's tabs at the mount root. A nested run appears as a directory below its parent.

## Directories

Metric tabs (`scalars`, `histograms`, `distributions`, `pr_curves`) contain training values and per-step tables; media tabs (`images`, `audio`, `videos`) contain stored media.
`text` contains text summaries; `meshes` geometry; `tensors` tensor values; `graphs` model graphs and run metadata; `hparams` run settings; `custom_scalars/layout.json` layouts; and `plugins` other plugin data.
`projector` and `profile` include run-directory sidecar files when available.
`raw/<event-file>/<20-digit-byte-offset>.tfrecord` contains one complete original TFRecord frame; filenames identify byte offsets in source order.

## Events and formats

The tree reads TensorFlow 1/2, Keras, PyTorch and PyTorch Lightning, tensorboardX, and compatible TensorBoard event writers. It exposes scalar, histogram, distribution, PR-curve, image, audio, video, text, mesh, tensor, hyperparameter, custom-scalar, graph and plugin data. A typed preview may be absent for an unsupported or malformed payload; check `raw/` for the original frame.

Equivalent encodings are alternate views of the same logged values, not separate observations. For example, scalar `<tag>.json`, `.tsv`, `.csv` and `.npz` files contain the same table; tensor `.npy` and `.json` files preview the same tensor. Step-based files use zero-padded global steps. Equal-step scalar rows are kept in producer order.

Media files keep the stored bytes and are not transcoded. Extensions indicate likely formats, not guaranteed decodability. `.bin` files contain opaque original tensor or field bytes, not a whole event frame; they are not, by themselves, evidence of a model checkpoint or weights. Use `raw/` for complete event framing and unsupported types.
